generator_convention: Row generator with clockwise rate (s+d)/2, counterclockwise rate (s-d)/2, total exit rate s; s >= |d|.

claims.statement: For the three-state circulant CTMC Q(d,s), at d=0 and d=4pi/(sqrt(3) tau), with shared s and integer action scales c observed after each fixed interval tau, exp(c tau Q(0,s))=exp(c tau Q(d,s)) for every allowed c.
claims.basis: The nonstationary eigenvalues are -3s/2 +- i sqrt(3)d/2; H1 adds phase 2pi c over tau, so its sampled transition matrix equals H0 exactly.
limits: The stated d value is tied to the generator convention in CYCLE4_REPORT.md.

claims.statement: With any common initial law and any shared emission kernel, the two hypotheses induce identical transcript laws for every finite fixed or adaptive policy whose actions are integer-scaled Q and whose reads occur only after tau.
claims.basis: Every conditional transition kernel is identical, so fixed-word probabilities agree and adaptive transcript equality follows by induction on observed histories.
limits: This concerns the sampled input/output process, not equality of continuous-time paths or generators.

claims.statement: An added probe with phase alpha=c t/tau outside the integers has different transition kernels under H0 and H1. Half phase alpha=1/2 gives P0=Pi+rU and P1=Pi-rU.
claims.basis: Explicit semigroup exponentiation on the two-dimensional zero-sum subspace.
limits: A transition-kernel difference alone does not guarantee observable separation under state-independent emissions.

claims.statement: From a common uniform stationary reset and shared conditionally independent emissions, one read has the same marginal under both hypotheses. At a half-phase probe, two reads distinguish them whenever K_E=sum_y ||(I-11^T/3)f_y||^2>0, using the sign of Pr(Y0=Y1)-sum_y Pr(Y=y)^2.
claims.basis: The centered same-output correlations are +r K_E/3 under H0 and -r K_E/3 under H1.
limits: If K_E=0, outputs are state-independent and no action/timing probe can distinguish the generators through these emissions.

claims.statement: For finite output alphabet b and actual gap gamma=r K_E/3>0, N=O(b^2 gamma^-2 log(b/delta)) independent reset replicates suffice for the two-read sign test; no uniform finite N exists without an upper bound on s and positive lower bound on emission contrast.
claims.basis: Empirical same-output and marginal frequencies with Hoeffding concentration and a union bound.
limits: Charge one reset, one probe action, and two readouts per replicate (or two actions if no baseline read is available).

claims.statement: The alias is a concrete instance of the classical Markov embedding problem and behavioral equivalence in finite-state input/output systems; the note makes no novelty claim for either general framework.

not_claimed: A new solution to the Markov embedding problem.
Identification of an unobserved generator from integer-grid data.
Distinguishability under constant emissions or unbounded-rate/unbounded-noise families with finite samples.
